trends.name: Iran Strait of Hormuz Escalation
trends.summary: Trump administration intensifying pressure on Iran with Pentagon signaling decisive action in coming days, while EU allies (Italy, France, Spain) are actively denying US military support and access to airbases. Strait of Hormuz closure threatens global oil supply with prices holding above $100/barrel and gasoline hitting $4/gallon domestically, creating politically sensitive consumer pain.

trends.name: US Gasoline Prices Hit $4/Gallon
trends.summary: US retail gasoline averaged $4.018 per gallon as of March 30, up 85 cents year-over-year, representing an estimated $120 billion annualized drag on consumer disposable income (0.5 percentage points). This marks the first time above $4/gallon since August 2022 and signals deteriorating consumer purchasing power amid geopolitical tensions.

trends.name: Nvidia Semiconductor Dominance Strategy
trends.summary: Nvidia's $2 billion strategic stake in Marvell Technology and continued partnership signal aggressive vertical integration to secure semiconductor supply chain dominance. Marvell stock surged 9% on the news, reflecting investor confidence in Nvidia's expansion beyond GPUs and continued AI infrastructure momentum.

trends.name: Warren Buffett Portfolio Rebalancing
trends.summary: Buffett disclosed he sold Apple too aggressively and would buy more despite current market levels, while making tiny new investments and flagging uncertainty. His public statements on Gates/Epstein fallout and Berkshire's cautious stance signal shifting conviction levels amid valuation concerns and limited deployment opportunities.

trends.name: Asian Market Weakness & Nikkei Decline
trends.summary: Nikkei 225 posted its worst month since October 2008 with a -12% decline, signaling broad emerging market distress amid geopolitical tensions and possible yen weakness. This reflects widening risk-off sentiment globally as the Iran escalation impacts international equities and growth expectations.

trends.name: McCormick-Unilever Foods $44.8B Mega-Merger
trends.summary: McCormick's acquisition of Unilever's food business at nearly $45 billion valuation signals consolidation in packaged food sector despite investor concerns about execution risk. Deal reflects appetite for scale in CPG markets but carries questions about integration complexity and market saturation.

trends.name: Inflation Expectations Softening
trends.summary: 1-year inflation swap at 3.3% and 30-year at 2.3% near 52-week lows signals market pricing in disinflation despite elevated gasoline prices. This divergence suggests traders see transitory energy shock rather than structural inflation, supporting bonds and limiting Fed hiking expectations.

trends.name: Qualcomm Semiconductor Deterioration
trends.summary: Qualcomm downgraded amid widening operational cracks in smartphone and 5G chip markets, signaling competitive pressures from both Nvidia and Asian competitors. Sector weakness contrasts with Nvidia's dominance, indicating bifurcated semiconductor strength around AI vs. traditional chips.

trends.name: Novo Nordisk Obesity Drug Competition Intensifies
trends.summary: Novo Nordisk launches multi-month Wegovy subscription model to compete with Eli Lilly's rapid market gains in obesity treatment. This pricing and packaging strategy shift signals pressure on margins and market share as competition commoditizes GLP-1 drug access and Lilly's aggressive pricing advantage.

trends.name: PayPal Underperformance & Valuation Concerns
trends.summary: PayPal downgraded despite undervaluation thesis due to persistent checkout weakness and declining earnings, signaling structural challenges in fintech payment processing. Weakness reflects broader e-commerce headwinds and competitive pressure from Square, Stripe, and other payment processors.

trends.name: Apple Midlife Crisis & Strategic Renewal
trends.summary: Apple faces maturity challenge at 50 as growth slows and must rely on AI integration and services expansion to reignite investor enthusiasm. Buffett's selective appetite for Apple despite recent selling highlights valuation concerns and questions about innovation pipeline sustainability.

trends.name: Credit Card APRs Impacting Consumer Spending
trends.summary: Boston Fed research confirms credit card APRs have 'economically meaningful' impact on consumer spending, signaling credit tightening headwinds during inflationary period. Combined with gasoline price shock, higher borrowing costs are compressing discretionary consumer demand and signaling recessionary risks.
